definition_zh: 转基因的；有外来基因引入的（生物）
definition_en: containing genes that have been deliberately transferred from another organism by genetic engineering
core_image: 一段从别的生物身上剪下来的基因，被送进一颗种子，长出带着外来血统的新苗
scene: 转基因作物的话题常在新闻里出现，标签、安全、口味各有争论。Growers debate how a transgenic crop changes the food supply.
sceneCN: 这里 transgenic 是「转基因的」（第 1 个义项：生物体内带有人工转入外来基因）；句意：超市给架上的每一种转基因作物贴上了标签。

pos.zh: 转基因的；有外来基因引入的
转基因生物；转基因品种

derivatives.zh: transgenic 的复数式名词用法，指转基因技术或转基因生物；由形容词名词化而来，义为「转基因学」
由前缀 trans-、词根 gene 与词尾 -e 构成，义为「转基因」即被转入的外来基因
由前缀 trans- 与希腊词根 genesis（发生）构成，义为「转基因作用」

senses.title: Carrying a transferred gene
senses.definition: describing an organism whose cells contain a gene introduced from a different kind of organism, usually by laboratory techniques
senses.definitionCN: 指细胞里含有人工转入的其他物种基因的生物（通常靠实验室技术）
senses.example: The lab keeps a line of transgenic mice for research.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室养着一系转基因小鼠用于研究。
senses.why: The trans- part means across, so a transgenic organism quite literally carries a gene that has crossed over from another species.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 trans- 意为「跨过去」，所以转基因生物字面上就携带着一个从别的物种那边跨过来的基因。

senses.title: A plant grown from engineered seed
senses.definition: a crop or food plant developed by genetic engineering, often to resist pests or tolerate herbicide
senses.definitionCN: 通过基因工程培育的作物或食用植物，常用来抗虫或耐除草剂
senses.example: Farmers debated whether to plant transgenic corn this season.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们争论这个季节是否要种转基因玉米。
senses.why: The farm-level meaning grows out of the first sense, because fields are where the altered seeds first become visible.
senses.whyCN: 田间义项从第一个义项长出来，因为被改动的种子最先是在农田里被人看见的。

senses.title: An animal model with an added gene
senses.definition: an animal, usually a mouse, modified to carry an extra gene so scientists can study a disease or a protein
senses.definitionCN: 经过改造、多带一个基因的动物（通常是小鼠），供科学家研究疾病或某种蛋白质
senses.example: Researchers injected the embryo and produced a transgenic mouse.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员注射了胚胎，得到了一只转基因小鼠。
senses.why: The same mechanism serves laboratories, where an extra gene is used as a switch to watch how a body works.
senses.whyCN: 同一种机制也服务于实验室：多出来的那个基因被当成开关，用来观察身体怎样运作。

senses.title: Food and public debate
senses.titleCN: 转基因食品与公众争论
senses.definition: the term for foods and products that have been genetically modified, often said with caution about safety or labelling
senses.definitionCN: 指经过基因改造的食品和产品，常带谨慎语气，涉及安全或标签问题
senses.example: Many shoppers avoid transgenic food and look for an organic label.
senses.exampleCN: 许多顾客回避转基因食品，转而寻找有机标签。
senses.why: Once transgenic products reach a shop shelf, a scientific label turns into a social topic, which is why the word now carries debate.
senses.whyCN: 一旦转基因产品上了商店货架，科学标签就变成了社会话题，所以这个词现在带着争论的色彩。

intro.en: Transgenic is a scientific compound of the twentieth century, built from the Latin prefix trans- (across) and the modern word gene, which comes from Greek genos (birth, kind).
intro.cn: transgenic 是二十世纪的科学复合词，由拉丁语前缀 trans-（跨越）加上现代词 gene（基因）构成，而 gene 本身又源自希腊语 genos（出生、种类）。

items.en: Trans means across or beyond, and the same prefix appears in transfer and transport.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为跨越、越过，与 transfer、transport 中的前缀相同。

items.en: Greek genos means birth, race, or kind, and gives the -gen- element in gene and genetics.
items.cn: 希腊语 genos 意为出生、种族、种类，是 gene 与 genetics 中 -gen- 成分的来源。

items.en: The Danish botanist Wilhelm Johannsen introduced the word gene for the unit of heredity.
items.cn: 丹麦植物学家约翰森提出 gene 一词，用来指遗传单位。

items.en: Compound adjectives in -genic, such as mutagenic and carcinogenic, spread in English science writing.
items.cn: 英语科学写作中，mutagenic、carcinogenic 这类以 -genic 结尾的复合形容词开始流行。

items.en: Genetic engineering made the idea of moving a gene between species practical, and transgenic was formed to describe the result.
items.cn: 基因工程让跨物种转移基因变得可行，transgenic 随之被造出来描述这种结果。

items.en: Today transgenic covers laboratory animals, farm crops, and public debate about food safety.
items.cn: 今天 transgenic 覆盖实验室动物、农田作物以及围绕食品安全的公众争论。

note.en: Transgenic looks close to transgene, transmissible, and transitory, and it sits near genetically modified in meaning.
note.cn: transgenic 在拼写上靠近 transgene、transmissible、transitory，在语义上又紧邻「基因改造」这一说法。

entries.definition: a gene introduced into a new organism
entries.definitionCN: 转入新生物体内的外来基因；同源名词

entries.definition: the science of making transgenic organisms
entries.definitionCN: 转基因技术或转基因学；派生形式

entries.definition: able to be passed from one person to another
entries.definitionCN: 可传染的、可流传的；共享前缀 trans-

entries.definition: changed by genetic engineering, the broader everyday phrase
entries.definitionCN: 经过基因改造的，是日常更宽泛的说法

entries.definition: designed and built by human technique
entries.definitionCN: 经人工设计的；强调技术介入

entries.definition: an offspring of two different species or varieties
entries.definitionCN: 杂交的、混合的；指两个物种杂交产生的后代

normalIntro.en: Transgenic combines trans- (across) with gene in the sense of a gene that crosses over from one organism.
normalIntro.cn: transgenic 把表示「跨越」的 trans- 与 gene 组合在一起，指跨过来、落到新生物身上的那个基因。

normal.en: The word is trans plus genic, meaning a gene has crossed over into a new body.
normal.cn: 这个词是 trans 加 genic，意思是有一个基因跨越到了新的身体里。

normal.en: Transgenic crops are common in farm news because the seeds are changed before planting.
normal.cn: 转基因作物在农业新闻里很常见，因为种子在播种前就被改动了。

normal.en: A transgenic mouse is a standard tool for studying human diseases.
normal.cn: 转基因小鼠是研究人类疾病的标准工具。

normal.en: The same trans- appears in transfer and transport, always pointing across.
normal.cn: 同样的 trans- 也出现在 transfer 与 transport 里，总是表示从一个地方到另一个地方。

normal.en: Genetically modified is the broader label; transgenic stresses the gene that crossed over.
normal.cn: 基因改造是更宽泛的标签，transgenic 则强调那个跨过来的基因。

abstract.en: Picture scissors cutting a gene from one plant and slipping it into another.
abstract.cn: 想象一把剪刀从一个植物上剪下基因，再把它塞进另一个植物里。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny passport stamped on a seed, marking it as foreign.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗种子上盖了一个小护照章，标明它来自外地。

abstract.en: See a supermarket shelf where every box wears a small warning label.
abstract.cn: 想象超市货架，每个盒子上都贴着一个小小的提醒标签。

examples.en: The team bred a transgenic plant that resists drought.
examples.cn: 该团队培育出一种耐旱的转基因植物。

examples.en: Some countries require a label on every transgenic food product.
examples.cn: 有些国家要求每个转基因食品都贴标签。

examples.en: Transgenic animals are widely used to test new medicines.
examples.cn: 转基因动物被广泛用于测试新药。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿丝基因」——把一段基因像穿丝线一样穿进另一颗种子里，这就是转基因；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语前缀 trans-（跨越、越过）+ 现代词 gene（基因，源自希腊语 genos 出生的种类）+ 形容词词尾 -ic，核心义「带着跨物种来的基因」。

sensesIntro.en: Transgenic starts as a laboratory label for an organism with a crossed-over gene, then spreads to farm crops, to animal models, and finally to a food debate.
sensesIntro.cn: transgenic 起先是实验室里描述「有跨过来基因」的生物的标签，随后扩展到农田作物、动物模型，最后进入食品争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gene cut from one organism and sewn into another.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一种生物身上剪下的基因，被缝进另一种生物里。

branches.en: The basic laboratory sense: a cell carrying a gene from elsewhere.
branches.cn: 基础实验义：细胞里带着来自别处的基因。

branches.en: The farm sense where altered seeds become crops.
branches.cn: 农田义：被改动的种子长成作物。

branches.en: The animal sense used in medical research.
branches.cn: 医学研究中的动物义项。

branches.en: The social sense that appears once products reach consumers.
branches.cn: 社会义项：产品到达消费者手中后出现。

branches.en: Food crops tie the field and the shop shelf together in the same debate.
branches.cn: 食用作物把农田与商店货架拉进同一场争论。

intro.en: Transgenic is built from the Latin prefix trans-, the modern root gene, and the adjective ending -ic, and it has given rise to transgene and transgenesis.
intro.cn: transgenic 由拉丁语前缀 trans-、现代词根 gene 与形容词词尾 -ic 拼成，后来又衍生出 transgene 与 transgenesis。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across or beyond; Greek genos, behind gene, means birth or kind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为跨越、越过；gene 背后的希腊语 genos 意为出生或种类。

items.example: The prefix trans- marks a crossing over.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 标记一次跨越。

items.example: Gene names the unit that is moved.
items.exampleCN: gene 指被搬运的那个遗传单位。

items.meaning: producing or produced by a gene
items.example: -genic links the word to other science terms.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -genic 把这个词与其他科学术语联系起来。
词尾 -ic 构成形容词。
transgenic 描述被改造过的生物。

items.example: A transgene is the traveller itself.
items.exampleCN: transgene 指那个被搬运过来的基因。

items.meaning: the act of introducing a gene
items.exampleCN: transgenesis 指整个操作过程。

items.example: Transgenics is the study built on these practices.
items.exampleCN: transgenics 指由这些实践形成的学问。

definition_zh: 短暂的；转瞬即逝的；临时的；短暂的过客
definition_en: lasting only a short time, or a person who stays in a place for only a short while
core_image: 匆匆经过的身影：一个影子从门口一闪而过，没留下任何脚印
scene: 夏日傍晚的雷雨来得快去得也快，几分钟后地面就干了。The power cut tonight was transient and lights soon came back.
sceneCN: 这里 transient 是「短暂的」（第 1 个义项：只持续很短时间）；句意：今晚的停电很短暂，灯很快就恢复了。

pos.zh: 短暂的；转瞬即逝的；临时的
短暂的事物；临时的过客

derivatives.zh: transient 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「短暂性；转瞬即逝」
transient 以 -y 替换 -ce 得到的另一种名词形式，义为「短暂」
transient 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「短暂地」

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: continuing for only a short period and then passing
senses.definitionCN: 只持续很短一段时间便过去
senses.example: The relief was transient, because the fever returned by midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这种缓解是短暂的，因为到午夜又发烧了。
senses.why: The Latin source means to go across, so whatever is transient simply passes through without settling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「穿过」，所以短暂的东西只是穿过而不停留。

senses.title: A passing person
senses.definition: a person who stays in a place only for a short time, such as a traveller or seasonal worker
senses.definitionCN: 只在一个地方停留很短时间的人，如旅客或季节工
senses.example: The hotel is filled with transients during the summer festival.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季庆典期间，旅馆里住满匆匆来去的过客。
senses.why: Because the adjective names what passes, it can turn into a noun for the person who passes through a town.
senses.whyCN: 既然形容词指「经过的东西」，它就自然转作名词，指那个经过城镇的人。

senses.title: A short electrical or physical pulse
senses.definition: a brief surge or fluctuation in a current, signal, or pressure that dies away quickly
senses.definitionCN: 电流、信号或压力中迅速衰减的短暂冲击或波动
senses.example: Engineers add a device to protect the circuit from a transient.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师加装一个装置，保护电路免受瞬时脉冲冲击。
senses.why: Technical use keeps the passing idea and makes it measurable, a change that appears and fades in an instant.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法保留「经过」的意象，并把它变成可测量的量：瞬间出现又消退的变化。

senses.title: Temporary or passing in nature
senses.definition: temporary and not fixed, as with a passing population or a short-lived arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 临时的、不固定的，如流动的人口或短暂存在的安排
senses.example: The city has a large transient labor force every harvest season.
senses.exampleCN: 每到收获季，这座城市就有一大批临时劳动力。
senses.why: The short-time sense extends to people and arrangements, where nothing stays put for long.
senses.whyCN: 「时间短」的义项扩展到人与安排上，也就是没有什么事情会长期固定下来。

intro.en: Transient comes from Latin transire, to go across, a compound of trans (across) and ire (to go), and was used of things that pass.
intro.cn: transient 来自拉丁语 transire（越过、经过），由 trans（跨越）与 ire（走）复合而成，用来形容会过去的东西。

items.en: Ire means to go, and trans means across, so transire means to pass over.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ire 意为走，trans 意为跨越，因此 transire 意为越过、经过。

items.en: Transiens is the present participle, meaning going across or passing.
items.cn: transiens 是现在分词，意为「正穿过的、经过的」。

items.en: French passes the word onward as transitorie, still keeping the passing image.
items.cn: 法语把该词传下去，词形为 transitorie，仍保留「经过」的意象。

items.en: English first uses transient of things that last only a while.
items.cn: 英语最早用 transient 形容只持续一会儿的事物。

items.en: The noun sense for a passing lodger or traveller develops.
items.cn: 表示临时住客或过路旅客的名词义变得通行。

items.en: The word spreads into electrical engineering and social description.
items.cn: 这个词后来进入电气工程与社会描述领域。

note.en: Transient looks close to transit, transition, and transience, and it sits near temporary and fleeting in meaning.
note.cn: transient 在拼写上靠近 transit、transition、transience，在语义上又紧邻「临时的」「转瞬即逝的」。

entries.definition: the act of moving people or goods from place to place
the process of changing from one state to another
the quality of lasting only a short time
lasting for a limited time but possibly longer than a moment
entries.definitionCN: 临时的；限时的，比瞬时更长

entries.definition: passing very quickly, almost gone as it appears
lasting a very short time, often literary

normalIntro.en: Transient is built on trans (across) and ire (to go), so whatever is transient is on its way through.
normalIntro.cn: transient 由 trans（跨越）与 ire（走）构成，所以短暂的东西总是在经过的路上。

normal.en: The same trans and go appear to be at the heart of transit and transition.
normal.cn: 同样的「跨越」与「走」这一语义核心也出现在 transit 与 transition 中。

normal.en: A transient population includes tourists and seasonal workers rather than settled residents.
normal.cn: 流动人口包括游客和季节工，而不是长期定居的居民。

normal.en: Engineers call a brief current spike a transient, a passing surge.
normal.cn: 工程师把短暂的电流尖峰称作 transient，也就是一次过路冲击。

normal.en: The noun transients often makes sense for people passing through a hotel or station.
normal.cn: 名词 transients 常指经过旅馆或车站的人。

normal.en: Compare temporary for something fixed in length, and fleeting for something gone at once.
normal.cn: 对比 temporary 指有明确时长的临时，fleeting 指瞬间消失。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow crossing a lit doorway and going on.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子穿过亮着的门口，继续往前走。

abstract.en: Imagine footprints in wet sand being washed away by one wave.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沙上的脚印被一个浪抹掉。

abstract.en: See a voltage spike on an oscilloscope screen, rising and falling at once.
abstract.cn: 想象示波器屏幕上一条电压尖峰，立刻升起来又降下去。

examples.en: The joy of the holiday was real but transient.
examples.cn: 节日的快乐是真的，却转瞬即逝。

examples.en: The hospital serves many transients who move with the harvest.
examples.cn: 这家医院服务许多随收获季节流动的人。

examples.en: A transient spike in prices worried the market for a few days.
examples.cn: 价格的一次短暂飙升让市场担心了几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「传薪特」——消息传得又快，像薪火一样一阵就过去，转瞬即逝；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（跨越）+ ire（走）→ transire（越过、经过）→ transiens（经过的）→ 法语 transitoire → 英语 transient，核心义「经过而不停留」。

sensesIntro.en: Transient begins with things that last only a moment, extends to people who pass through a place, to measurable pulses in engineering, and to whatever is not fixed or lasting.
sensesIntro.cn: transient 从只持续片刻的事物开始，扩展到经过一个地方的人、工程中可测量的脉冲，以及一切不固定、不长久的安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shadow crossing a doorway and moving on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子穿过门口，继续往前走。

branches.en: The basic sense of passing in a moment.
branches.cn: 基本义：片刻之间就过去。

branches.en: The noun for a person passing through a place.
branches.cn: 名词义：经过某地的人。

branches.en: The technical sense of a pulse that dies away quickly.
branches.cn: 技术义：迅速衰减的脉冲。

branches.en: The general sense of what is temporary and not fixed.
branches.cn: 泛指临时、不固定的安排。

branches.en: A passing population turns a short stay into a social fact.
branches.cn: 流动人口把短暂的停留变成一种社会事实。

intro.en: Transient comes from trans- and ire, and English builds transience, transiency, and transiently on top of it.
intro.cn: transient 来自 trans- 与 ire，英语在此基础上又构成 transience、transiency 与 transiently。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across and ire means to go, giving transire to pass over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为跨越，ire 意为走，合起来是 transire，意为越过、经过。

items.example: The prefix trans- points to crossing over.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 指向跨越。
ire 提供「行进」的意思。

items.meaning: being in a state of doing
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ient 标记形容词。
词尾 -ence 构成 transience。
词尾 -ency 构成 transiency。
词尾 -ly 构成 transiently。
transient 描述会经过的事物。
transience 指短暂这种性质。

definition_zh: 运输；通行；经过；中转；天文凌日
definition_en: the movement of people or goods from one place to another, or the passage of a body through a place
core_image: 一辆满载货物的车从一站出发，穿过长长的路线，到达下一站
scene: 港口的集装箱在仓库与码头之间来回搬运，一座城市的地铁也日夜运行。Goods in transit must be kept cool.
sceneCN: 这里 transit 是「运输、在途」（第 1 个义项：人或货物从一处移到另一处）；句意：运输途中的货物必须保持低温。

pos.zh: 通过；经过；（天体）从另一天体前面经过

derivatives.zh: transit 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「过渡；转变」
由词根 trans- 与形容词词尾 -ive 构成，义为「及物的；传递的」
由词根 trans- 加词尾 -ory 构成，义为「短暂的」
transitive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「及物地；传递地」

senses.title: Carrying from one place to another
senses.definition: the act of moving people or goods from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把人或货物从一处运送到另一处的行为
senses.example: The port handles the transit of millions of containers each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口每年处理数百万个集装箱的转运。
senses.why: Transit comes from transire, to go across, so the word names the movement itself.
senses.whyCN: transit 来自 transire（越过），所以这个词直接指「移动」这件事本身。

senses.title: Passage through a place
senses.definition: the state of passing through a country, city, or station on the way elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在去往别处的路上经过某国、某城或某站的状态
senses.example: Refugees passed in transit through the border town.
senses.exampleCN: 难民们过境经过这个边境小镇。
senses.why: This sense follows the same movement: nothing is carried, the body or cargo simply crosses on the way.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思顺着「移动」延伸而来：并不强调搬运，只强调身体或货物在途中穿过去。

senses.title: A public transport system
senses.definition: the network of buses, trains, and other transport used by the public
senses.definitionCN: 由公交、地铁等构成的公众使用的交通网络
senses.example: The city is building a new transit line to the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 该市正在修建通往机场的新公交线。
senses.why: Once many people make the same crossing every day, the passage becomes a system with lines and timetables.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人每天走同一条路线时，那次次穿越就变成有线路和时刻表的系统。

senses.title: A body crossing another
senses.definition: the passage of one celestial body across the face of another, or a crossing in front of it
senses.definitionCN: 一个天体从另一个天体前面穿过的天文现象
senses.example: Astronomers recorded the transit of Venus across the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家记录下金星凌日的现象。
senses.why: Looking up at the sky, a planet in front of the sun repeats the same crossing on a much larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 抬头看天空，行星走到太阳前面的样子，就是同一种穿越在宇宙尺度上的重演。

intro.en: Transit comes from Latin transitus, a going across, from transire, built on trans (across) and ire (to go).
intro.cn: transit 来自拉丁语 transitus（越过），源于 transire，由 trans（跨越）与 ire（走）构成。

items.en: Ire means to go, and trans means across, so transire means to pass over.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ire 意为走，trans 意为跨越，因此 transire 意为越过、经过。

items.en: The noun transitus means a passing or a going across.
items.cn: 名词 transitus 意为经过、越过。

items.en: French transit carries the word on in the sense of passage.
items.cn: 法语 transit 以「经过」的意义把这个词传下去。

items.en: English adopts transit for passing through a place or a matter.
items.cn: 英语借用 transit，表示经过某地或某事物。

items.en: With trains and tramways the word shifts toward public transport and in transit.
items.cn: 随着火车与有轨电车出现，这个词转向公共交通与运输途中。

items.en: Astronomy and geography add the crossing of a planet or moon.
items.cn: 天文学与地理学又增添了行星或卫星从前面穿过的用法。

note.en: Transit looks close to transition, transitory, and transitive, and it sits near transit line and passage in meaning.
note.cn: transit 在拼写上靠近 transition、transitory、transitive，在语义上又与交通线、通道相邻。

entries.definition: the process of changing from one state to another
describing a verb that takes a direct object
relating to a change or a period between two states
entries.definitionCN: 过渡的；过渡期的；派生形式

entries.definition: the system or act of carrying goods and people
the act of moving through something
a regular journey between home and work

normalIntro.en: Transit joins trans (across) with ire (to go): the word is the going itself, the journey from one point to the next.
normalIntro.cn: transit 把「跨越」的 trans 与「走」的 ire 放在一起：这个词就是「走」这件事本身，从一点到另一点的行程。

normal.en: In transit is the everyday phrase for goods on their way.
normal.cn: in transit 是货物在途时的日常说法。

normal.en: Public transit covers buses, trains, and ferries used by everyone.
normal.cn: public transit 包括人人可用的公交、地铁与渡轮。

normal.en: The related transition shifts the stress to the second syllable.
normal.cn: 相关的 transition 重音移到第二个音节。

normal.en: The verb transits appears in such phrases as the planet transits the sun.
normal.cn: 动词 transits 见于 the planet transits the sun 这类说法。

normal.en: Compare transport, which stresses carrying, with transit, which stresses passing through.
normal.cn: 对比 transport 强调搬运，transit 强调穿过。

abstract.en: Picture a truck rolling through a tunnel from one valley to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车穿过隧道，从一个山谷开往下一个山谷。

abstract.en: Imagine a small dark dot sliding across the face of the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小黑点滑过太阳表面。

abstract.en: Watch a line of buses on a map, each one a moving segment.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一串公交线路，每一段都在移动。

examples.en: The goods were damaged in transit.
examples.cn: 货物在运输途中损坏了。

examples.en: Public transit in the city is cheap and reliable.
examples.cn: 这座城市的公共交通便宜又可靠。

examples.en: Scientists observed the transit of the planet across the sun.
examples.cn: 科学家观测到这颗行星凌日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿西特」——穿过一条西边的大街，很快就到了特别的地方；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（跨越）+ ire（走）→ transire（越过）→ 名词 transitus（经过）→ 法语 transit → 英语 transit，核心义「穿过、经过」。

sensesIntro.en: Transit starts as the carrying of goods across space, extends to passage through a place, to the system that moves the public, and to a sky body crossing another.
sensesIntro.cn: transit 起先是把货物从一处搬运到另一处，随后扩展到经过一个地方、搬运公众的交通系统，以及天体从另一个天体前面穿过。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loaded truck passing through a long route from one stop to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆满载的卡车沿长路线从一站开到下一站。

branches.en: The core sense of carrying people or goods.
branches.cn: 核心义：搬运人或货物。

branches.en: The sense of passing through a place on the way.
branches.cn: 义项二：路上穿过某地。

branches.en: The sense of a public transport network.
branches.cn: 义项三：公共交通网络。

branches.en: The astronomical sense of a body crossing another.
branches.cn: 义项四：天体从另一天体前穿过。

branches.en: A transport system is carrying made into a daily network.
branches.cn: 交通系统就是把搬运变成日常网络。

intro.en: Transit is trans plus ire, and it feeds transition, transitive, and transitory, each pressing the idea of crossing in a different direction.
intro.cn: transit 由 trans 加 ire 构成，又衍生出 transition、transitive 与 transitory，各自把「穿过」推向不同方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across and ire means to go; transire and its noun transitus supply the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为跨越，ire 意为走；transire 及其名词 transitus 提供了这个词。

items.example: The prefix trans- marks a crossing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 标记穿越。

items.example: Ire adds the idea of motion.
items.exampleCN: ire 加上移动的意思。
transit 指这段行程。
词尾 -ion 构成 transition。
词尾 -ive 构成 transitive。
词尾 -ory 构成 transitory。
词尾 -ly 构成 transitively。

items.meaning: a change from one state to another
items.exampleCN: transition 保留「穿越」的意象。

definition_zh: 短暂的；暂时的；转瞬即逝的；（法律）临时的
definition_en: lasting only for a short time and then passing away
core_image: 一队旅人穿过营地，搭起帐篷又拆走，只留下脚印
scene: 清晨的公园草坪上，露水还挂在草尖，太阳一出来就蒸发了。The dew on the grass in the park is transitory, gone before anyone notices.
sceneCN: 这里 transitory 是「短暂的、转瞬即逝的」（第 1 个义项：存在时间很短、随后就消失）；句意：公园草坪上的露珠转瞬即逝，还没等人留意就消失了。

pos.zh: 短暂的；暂时的；转瞬即逝的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「短暂；短暂的特性」
同出拉丁语 transire，义为「通过；过境；运输」，核心是「穿过」
拉丁语 transire 的名词形式 transitus，义为「过渡；转变」
同源形容词，义为「短暂的；瞬时的」，比 transitory 更常用于技术语境
形近陷阱：由 transitive（及物的）派生，义为「及物地」，与「短暂」无关

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: existing or continuing for only a short period before ending
senses.definitionCN: 只存在或持续很短一段时间便结束
senses.example: The beauty of cherry blossom is famously transitory.
senses.exampleCN: 樱花之美是出了名的短暂。
senses.why: The Latin verb transire means to pass over or go past, so anything transitory literally passes by.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 transire 意为「经过、通过」，所以 transitory 描述的事物本质上就是「过一趟就走」的。

senses.title: An intermediate stage
senses.definition: belonging to a period between a starting point and a finished state, especially in psychology or politics
senses.definitionCN: 处于起点与完成状态之间的中间阶段，尤用于心理学或政治语境
senses.example: Economists describe the current downturn as a transitory phase in the cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把当前的衰退描述为周期中的过渡阶段。
senses.why: Passing through is also passing from one stage to the next, so the word marks an in-between period.
senses.whyCN: 「经过」也意味着从一个阶段走向下一个阶段，于是这个词可以标出一个夹在中间的时期。

senses.title: Darkness of the memory
senses.definition: a sudden brief loss of consciousness or memory, an older medical usage
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂的意识或记忆丧失，属较早的医学用法
senses.example: Early doctors spoke of a transitory darkness falling on the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的医生谈到病人身上会突然降临一阵短暂的黑蒙。
senses.why: Older prose used the word for states that pass through a person, the mind momentarily leaving its usual place.
senses.whyCN: 较早的散文用这个词表示「穿过人身体的状态」，脑子里那种片刻的空白被看作一种经过性的状态。

senses.title: Transient in law
senses.definition: in law, describing a right, claim, or person that is temporary or passing through a place
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，形容权利、主张或人只是暂时的或途经某地
senses.example: A transitory right passes with the property it is attached to.
senses.exampleCN: 临时性权利会随它所依附的财产一同转移。
senses.why: Legal writing borrowed the idea of passing through and used it for rights that travel with the property.
senses.whyCN: 法律写作借用了「经过」的观念，用它描述那些随财产一同流转的权利。

senses.title: Not permanent in nature
senses.definition: contrasted with the eternal and the fixed, as in philosophical talk about life and things of this world
senses.definitionCN: 与永恒和固定相对，常用于哲学中谈论生命与世界之物
senses.example: The philosopher argued that all earthly goods are transitory.
senses.exampleCN: 那位哲学家主张，一切尘世之物都不能持久。
senses.why: The strongest contrast for a passing thing is the eternal, so the word became a staple of moral writing.
senses.whyCN: 会经过的东西最强烈的对照就是永恒，于是这个词成了道德与哲学写作的常用词。

senses.title: A passing mood
senses.definition: describing a feeling, mood, or interest that comes and goes quickly
senses.definitionCN: 形容来得快、去得也快的感受、情绪或兴趣
senses.example: Her irritation was transitory and vanished after a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她的不快只是一时的，喝杯茶后就消失了。
senses.why: Moods pass through the mind like travellers, which fits the core image of a stay that ends soon.
senses.whyCN: 情绪就像旅人一样从心中经过，这正契合「停留短暂便离开」的核心意象。

intro.en: Transitory comes from Latin transitorius, from transire, to pass over, built from trans, across, and ire, to go.
intro.cn: transitory 来自拉丁语 transitorius，源于 transire（经过），由 trans（穿过）与 ire（走）构成。

items.en: Ire means to go, the everyday verb of motion.
items.cn: ire 意为「走」，是拉丁语中最基本的移动动词。

items.en: Trans means across or over, and transire means to go across.
items.cn: trans 表示「横过、越过」，transire 就是「穿过、越过」。

items.en: Transitorius means passing through, or not lasting.
items.cn: 形容词 transitorius 表示「经过的、不能持久的」。

items.en: Scholastic writers keep the adjective in Latin, and French forms follow from it.
items.cn: 经院学者继续使用这个拉丁形容词，法语形式随之衍生。

items.en: The adjective enters English as transitorie with the sense of not lasting.
items.cn: 这个形容词以 transitorie 的形式进入英语，意为「不能持久的」。

items.en: Modern English fixes the spelling transitory and adds legal and economic uses.
items.cn: 现代英语固定为 transitory，并增加了法律与经济领域的用法。

note.en: Transitory belongs to the transire family of passing over, and sits near transient, ephemeral, and temporary.
note.cn: transitory 属于「经过」的 transire 词族，与 transient、ephemeral、temporary 语义相邻。

entries.definition: lasting only a short time, or a passing visitor
entries.definitionCN: 短暂的；过客；同源，比 transitory 更常用于技术与科学语境

entries.definition: a process of changing from one state to another
entries.definitionCN: 过渡；转变；同出 transire 的名词 transitus

entries.definition: describing a verb that takes a direct object
entries.definitionCN: 及物的（动词）；只是拼写相近，词源同为 transire 但语义分岔到语法

entries.definition: lasting for a limited time, often by arrangement
entries.definitionCN: 临时的；暂时的，常指有意安排的短期

entries.definition: lasting for a very short time
entries.definitionCN: 朝生暮死的；瞬息即逝的，语气更文雅

entries.definition: passing very quickly and soon forgotten
entries.definitionCN: 一闪而过的；稍纵即逝的

normalIntro.en: Transitory is the adjective of transire, to pass over, so its whole meaning is a stay that ends.
normalIntro.cn: transitory 是 transire（经过）的形容词形式，它的全部含义就是「一次会结束的停留」。

normal.en: Trans- means across, as in transport, so transitory marks what crosses and moves on.
normal.cn: trans- 表示「横穿」，如 transport；transitory 标记的正是穿过后就继续前行的东西。

normal.en: Transient and transitory share a root; use transitory for life and beauty, transient for forces and signals.
normal.cn: transient 与 transitory 同根；谈生命与美丽用 transitory，谈力与信号多用 transient。

normal.en: Of a transitory nature is a formal way to say something will not last.
normal.cn: of a transitory nature 是「不会持久」的正式说法。

normal.en: Its noun transitoriness names the quality of lasting briefly.
normal.cn: 它的名词 transitoriness 指「短暂性」这一性质。

normal.en: Compare temporary: temporary is neutral and practical, transitory is literary and carries a touch of sorrow.
normal.cn: 对比 temporary：temporary 中性而务实，transitory 更书面，带一丝惋惜。

abstract.en: Picture travellers pitching a tent at dusk and walking away at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人在黄昏搭起帐篷，天一亮又走开。

abstract.en: Picture dew on a blade of grass, drying as the sun climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象草叶上的露珠，太阳升高时一点点干掉。

abstract.en: Think of a film scene cut short in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一场电影在半途被剪短。

examples.en: Fame in the online world is often transitory, forgotten within weeks.
examples.cn: 网络世界的名声常常是短暂的，几周内就被遗忘。

examples.en: The doctor described the pain as transitory and unlikely to return.
examples.cn: 医生称这种疼痛只是暂时的，不太可能再犯。

examples.en: Families in a transitory settlement moved on as the season changed.
examples.cn: 过渡安置点的家庭随着季节变化而迁走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「串起来的临时集市」——摊子一摆就撤，热闹不过几天；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans（穿过）+ ire（走）→ transire（经过）→ transitorius（经过的、不能持久的）→ 英语 transitory，核心义「经过便走、无法久留」。

sensesIntro.en: Transitory starts as things that pass by quickly, then marks an in-between stage, and finally covers passing states, legal passing rights, and emotions that do not last.
sensesIntro.cn: transitory 先指很快经过的事物，再指标出一个中间阶段，最后覆盖经过性的状态、法律上的临时权利以及不能持久的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camp that is packed up the moment the travellers leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人一走就拆掉的营地。

branches.en: Things that last only a short time are the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 只存在很短时间的事物是日常义项。

branches.en: Passing from one stage to another gives the intermediate sense.
branches.cn: 从一个阶段过渡到下一个阶段，给出「中间阶段」的义项。

branches.en: The old medical usage names a state that passes through the patient.
branches.cn: 较早的医学用法指一种从病人身上经过的状态。

branches.en: Legal rights that pass with property and goods that are not eternal share the passing idea.
branches.cn: 随财产流转的法律权利与不能持久的尘世之物，都共享「经过」这一观念。

branches.en: Emotions that come and go also stay only briefly.
branches.cn: 来来去去的情绪同样只停留片刻。

intro.en: Transitory is built on the Latin prefix trans-, meaning across, and the verb ire, to go, with English relatives transit, transition, and transient.
intro.cn: transitory 由拉丁语前缀 trans-（横过）与动词 ire（走）构成，英语同族有 transit、transition 与 transient。

latinIntro.en: Latin transire means to go across, and its adjective transitorius means passing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 transire 意为「穿过」，其形容词 transitorius 意为「经过的」。

items.example: The prefix trans- adds the idea of crossing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 加上「穿越」之意。

items.example: Ire is the plain verb of going.
items.exampleCN: ire 是最基本的「走」的动词。

items.meaning: to go across, to pass over
items.exampleCN: transire 由 trans- 与 ire 合成。

items.example: Transitorius gives the English adjective its shape.
items.exampleCN: transitorius 给英语形容词提供了外形。

items.example: The ending -ory appears in many Latin adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 出现在许多拉丁形容词中。

items.meaning: the act of passing through a place
items.example: Transit keeps the sense of passing.
items.exampleCN: transit 保留了「经过」之义。

items.meaning: a change from one state to another
items.exampleCN: transition 命名了通过的过程本身。

items.example: Transient is the twin adjective of transitory.
items.exampleCN: transient 是 transitory 的孪生形容词。
词尾 -ness 构成 transitoriness。

items.example: Transitively comes from a different branch of sense.
items.exampleCN: transitively 来自另一条语义分支。

derivatives.zh: 短暂；短暂的性质
过渡；转变
短暂的；瞬时的

definition_zh: 发射机；发送器；（信号或病原体的）传播者；传递者
definition_en: a device or person that sends out signals, messages, or disease from one place to another
core_image: 山顶的铁塔把一道电波抛出去，穿过山谷送进远处的收音机
scene: 旧收音机的天线断了，屋里只剩下沙沙的杂音。Without a working transmitter, the station could not reach anyone beyond the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 transmitter 是「发射机、发送设备」（第 1 个义项：把信号发送出去的装置）；句意：没有一台正常工作的发射机，这家电台就无法覆盖山谷以外的任何人。

pos.zh: 传播者；传递者；（病原体）传播媒介

collocations.zh: 神经递质（神经传导物质）
手持发射器；手持遥控器

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「传送；传播；发射」，transmitter 由它加施事后缀 -er 构成
由 transmit 加拉丁名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「传送；传播；传输」
由 transmit 加 -ible 构成，义为「可传送的；可传染的」
neuro-（神经）+ transmitter，义为「神经递质」

senses.title: A device that sends signals
senses.definition: an electronic device that sends out radio, television, or other signals
senses.definitionCN: 发送无线电、电视等信号的电子装置
senses.example: The radio transmitter on the hill covers the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 山上的无线电发射机覆盖整个地区。
senses.why: The verb transmit sends something across, so the -er form names the thing doing the sending.
senses.whyCN: 动词 transmit 表示把某物送过一段距离，加 -er 就指名了「做发送这件事的东西」。

senses.title: One who carries something across
senses.definition: a person or group that passes a message, tradition, or idea on to others
senses.definitionCN: 把信息、传统或思想传给他人的人或群体
senses.example: Monks were the main transmitter of old manuscripts during that age.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个时代，修士是古代手稿的主要传递者。
senses.why: Sending is not only electrical; anyone who hands something on literally transmits it.
senses.whyCN: 「发送」不只限于电信号；任何把东西交到别人手上的人，本质上都在 transmit。

senses.title: A carrier of disease
senses.definition: an animal, insect, or person that carries a pathogen and passes it to others
senses.definitionCN: 携带病原体并把它传给他人或他物的动物、昆虫或人
senses.example: Mosquitoes are a common transmitter of malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是疟疾常见的传播媒介。
senses.why: The image of a channel that moves something from one body to another fits infection exactly.
senses.whyCN: 「把东西从一处输送到另一处」的渠道意象，正好对上了感染的传播路径。

senses.title: A relay in the body
senses.definition: a chemical substance that carries a nerve signal across a synapse, often in the compound neurotransmitter
senses.definitionCN: 在突触间传递神经信号的化学物质，多用于复合词 neurotransmitter
senses.example: Dopamine is a neurotransmitter that affects mood and movement.
senses.exampleCN: 多巴胺是一种影响情绪与运动的神经递质。
senses.why: Even inside the body, the message must be sent across a gap, so biology borrowed the same sending word.
senses.whyCN: 即使在身体内部，信息也要跨过一道缝隙才能传递，于是生物学借用了同一个「发送」词。

senses.title: The sending part of a set
senses.titleCN: （对讲设备的）发话端；遥控发射端
senses.definition: the part of a two-way device or remote control that sends rather than receives
senses.definitionCN: 双向设备或遥控装置中负责发送而非接收的那一部分
senses.example: Keep the transmitter within sight of the receiver while you test it.
senses.exampleCN: 测试时请让发射端保持在接收端视线之内。
senses.why: Pairs of devices split the work between sending and receiving, and the sending half gets the name.
senses.whyCN: 成对的设备把工作分为发送与接收，负责发送的那一半就得到了这个名字。

intro.en: Transmitter is English trans- (across) plus a Latin-derived mit plus the agent suffix -er, built on the verb transmit.
intro.cn: transmitter 由 trans-（穿过）＋源自拉丁语的 mit＋施事后缀 -er 构成，基础是动词 transmit。

items.en: Mit comes from mittere, to send or let go.
items.cn: mit 来自拉丁语 mittere，意为「送出、放走」。

items.en: Transmittere joins trans, across, with mittere, to send.
items.cn: transmittere 把 trans（横过）与 mittere（送）结合起来。

items.en: The verb transmit enters English as to send across or forward.
items.cn: 动词 transmit 进入英语，意为「传送过去、转交」。

items.en: Transmitter appears as the agent noun of transmit.
items.cn: transmitter 作为 transmit 的施事名词出现。

items.en: With telegraphy and wireless, the word shifts to the machine that sends signals.
items.cn: 随着电报与无线电问世，这个词转向指「发送信号的机器」。

items.en: Modern English adds medical uses for carriers of disease and nerve signals.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了指疾病与神经信号传递者的医学用法。

note.en: Transmitter is the agent noun of transmit, sitting beside receiver and broadcast, and close to carrier in medicine.
note.cn: transmitter 是 transmit 的施事名词，与 receiver、broadcast 配对使用，在医学中与 carrier 含义相近。

entries.definition: the act of sending or the signal sent
able to be sent or passed on
entries.definitionCN: 可传送的；可传染的；同根形容词

a station or person that sends out programmes

normalIntro.en: Transmitter is transmit plus -er, so the name belongs to whatever does the sending.
normalIntro.cn: transmitter 就是 transmit 加 -er，名字属于「负责发送的那一方」。

normal.en: Transmitter always pairs with receiver, the two halves of any signal system.
normal.cn: transmitter 总与 receiver 成对出现，是任何信号系统的两端。

normal.en: The base verb is transmit, the long noun is transmission, the short one is the sender itself.
normal.cn: 基础动词是 transmit，长名词是 transmission，短名词则指发送的那件东西本身。

normal.en: In medicine a transmitter carries a pathogen, as in a transmitter of malaria.
normal.cn: 医学中 transmitter 指携带病原体者，如 a transmitter of malaria（疟疾传播媒介）。

normal.en: Neurotransmitter simply puts neuro, for nerve, in front of the same word.
normal.cn: neurotransmitter 只是把表示「神经」的 neuro 加在同一个词前面。

normal.en: Compare transmit: transmit is the act, transmitter is the actor.
normal.cn: 对比 transmit：transmit 是动作，transmitter 是执行动作的一方。

abstract.en: Picture a steel tower flinging invisible ripples over a valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一座铁塔把看不见的波纹抛过整道山谷。

abstract.en: Picture a monk copying a manuscript and handing it along.
abstract.cn: 想象一位修士抄写手稿，再把它传给下一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito as a tiny delivery van for infection.
abstract.cn: 想象蚊子是一辆运送感染的微型货车。

examples.en: Engineers replaced the transmitter before the storm reached the coast.
examples.cn: 工程师在风暴抵达海岸前更换了发射机。

examples.en: Wild birds can act as a transmitter of the virus between farms.
examples.cn: 野鸟可以在农场之间充当病毒的传播媒介。

examples.en: Every transmitter in the network is checked twice a month.
examples.cn: 网络中的每台发射机每月都会被检查两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「传斯密特」——把消息一「传」就「密」密「特」别地送出去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans（横过）+ mittere（送）→ transmittere（传送）→ 英语动词 transmit → transmitter，核心义「把东西送过一段距离的那一方」。

sensesIntro.en: Transmitter begins with the machine that sends signals, extends to people who pass things on, then to carriers of disease and nerve signals, and finally to the sending half of a device.
sensesIntro.cn: transmitter 先指发送信号的机器，再扩展到传递消息的人，继而指疾病与神经信号的传递者，最后指设备中负责发送的一端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower that throws a signal across a valley.
core.cn: 核心意象：把信号抛过山谷的铁塔。

branches.en: The signal-sending machine is the primary technical sense.
branches.cn: 发送信号的机器是首要的技术义项。

branches.en: A person who passes things on is the human sending sense.
branches.cn: 把东西传下去的人是「人为发送」的义项。

branches.en: A carrier of disease is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 疾病的携带者是生物学义项。

branches.en: The broadcast machine and the sending half of a remote both name the active sender.
branches.cn: 广播机器与遥控器的发送一端，都指主动发出信号的一方。

branches.en: Disease agents and nerve chemicals both carry something across a gap.
branches.cn: 病原体与神经化学物质都在把某物送过一道缝隙。

intro.en: Transmitter combines trans-, meaning across, the root mit from Latin mittere, to send, and the English agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: transmitter 由表示「横过」的 trans-、拉丁语 mittere（送）的词根 mit，以及英语施事后缀 -er 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere means to send, and transmittere means to send across.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送」，transmittere 意为「送过去」。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 标示横向移动。

items.exampleCN: mittere 是 mit- 的词根。

transmittere 由 trans 与 mittere 合成。

items.example: The suffix -er forms transmitter from transmit.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 transmit 变为 transmitter。

items.example: Transmission names the act rather than the agent.
items.exampleCN: transmission 指行为而非施事者。
前缀 neuro- 构成 neurotransmitter。

items.exampleCN: neurotransmitter 是身体版的 transmitter。

definition_zh: 使转变；使蜕变；（炼金术中）使（金属）转化
definition_en: to change something completely into another form, substance, or nature
core_image: 铅块在坩埚里熔开，冷却后变成一块发亮的金子
scene: 古老的实验室里，炼金术士整夜守着炉火，等待坩埚中的变化。Legend says the old alchemists tried to transmute lead into gold.
sceneCN: 这里 transmute 是「使转变、使转化」（第 1 个义项：把一种物质彻底变成另一种物质）；句意：传说古代炼金术士试图把铅变成金子。

collocations.zh: 使一种元素转变为另一种元素

derivatives.zh: 由 transmute 加拉丁名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「转变；蜕变；（核）嬗变」
由 transmute 加 -able 构成，义为「可转变的；可转化的」
transmute 加 -er 构成，义为「使转变者」（对应拉丁语 transmutare 的直接来源）
同出拉丁语 mutare（改变），义为「突变；变异」
同出 mutare，加 com-（共同）构成，义为「通勤；减刑」

senses.title: To change into another substance
senses.definition: to change one substance completely into a different one, as in alchemy
senses.definitionCN: 把一种物质彻底变成另一种物质，如炼金术所为
senses.example: The alchemist hoped to transmute lead into gold.
senses.exampleCN: 那位炼金术士希望把铅变成金子。
senses.why: Trans- means across and mutare means to change, so transmute is to change a thing all the way across into something else.
senses.whyCN: trans- 表示「横过」，mutare 表示「改变」，所以 transmute 就是把一样东西一路变过界，成为另一样东西。

senses.title: To turn one element into another
senses.definition: in physics, to convert an atom of one element into an atom of a different element
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中，使某元素的原子转变为另一元素的原子
senses.example: Accelerators can transmute one element into another entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 加速器可以让一种元素完全变成另一种元素。
senses.why: Modern physics found a real transmutation, so alchemists became chemistry and their dream a laboratory fact.
senses.whyCN: 现代物理学找到了真实的「转变」，炼金术化作化学，而炼金者的梦想成了实验室里的事实。

senses.title: To change the nature of something
senses.definition: to change the character or essence of something, not just its surface
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物的性质或本质，而不只是表面
senses.example: Grief can transmute an easy manner into something guarded.
senses.exampleCN: 悲伤能把自在的举止变成一种自我防卫。
senses.why: If a metal can turn into another metal, then a feeling or a talent can turn into another nature.
senses.whyCN: 金属既然能变成另一种金属，情绪与才能自然也能变成另一种性质。

senses.title: To convert into a new form
senses.definition: to turn energy, data, or ideas from one form into a usable form
senses.definitionCN: 把能量、数据或想法从一种形式转变成可用的形式
senses.example: The engine transmutes heat into motion.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机把热量转化成运动。
senses.why: The same change across applies to any form that is converted into another usable one.
senses.whyCN: 同样这种「跨过去变一次」的动作，也适用于任何被转换成另一种可用状态的东西。

senses.title: To become something else
senses.definition: used without an object, to change oneself into a different state or shape
senses.definitionCN: 不带宾语使用，指自身变为另一种状态或形态
senses.example: Over the years the harbour transmuted into a shopping quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 这些年港湾逐渐变成了购物街区。
senses.why: The verb can lose its object and describe the whole thing changing from inside.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以不带宾语，用来描述整个事物从内部发生改变。

intro.en: Transmute comes from Latin transmutare, built from trans, across, and mutare, to change, and the same mutare root gives mutate and commute.
intro.cn: transmute 来自拉丁语 transmutare，由 trans（横过）与 mutare（改变）构成，同样的 mutare 也生出 mutate 与 commute。

items.en: Mutare means to change or exchange.
items.cn: mutare 意为「改变、交换」。

items.en: Transmutare means to change something into another form.
items.cn: transmutare 意为「把某物变成另一种形态」。

items.en: The noun transmutatio names that change over.
items.cn: 名词 transmutatio 命名这种「变过去」的过程。

items.en: Alchemy gives the word its famous use, the changing of base metal into gold.
items.cn: 炼金术赋予这个词最著名的用法：把贱金属变成黄金。

items.en: Transmute enters English from Medieval Latin, first in alchemical writing.
items.cn: transmute 从中世纪拉丁语进入英语，最早见于炼金术文本。

items.en: The word widens to cover energy, ideas, and nuclear change.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到能量、思想以及核物理的变化。

note.en: Transmute is the strong verb of change from one nature to another, close to its root relatives mutate and mutual, and to everyday verbs like convert and transform.
note.cn: transmute 是「彻底改变性质」的强势动词，与同根的 mutate、mutual 相邻，也与日常的 convert、transform 意义相近。

entries.definition: the act of changing into another form
able to be changed into another form
to change in form, especially in genetics
entries.definitionCN: 突变；变异；同为拉丁语 mutare 的后代

entries.definition: shared or experienced by two sides
entries.definitionCN: 相互的；共同的；同根但走的是「交换」那一支

entries.definition: to change into another form or use
entries.definitionCN: 转变；转换；更强调用途与形式的改变

entries.definition: to change the form or appearance greatly
to change shape completely, as an insect does
entries.definitionCN: 变态；彻底蜕变；多用于生物

normalIntro.en: Transmute is a Latin word made of two clear pieces, trans for across and mute from mutare for change.
normalIntro.cn: transmute 是一个拉丁式合成词，由两块清晰的部件组成：trans 表示「横过」，mute 来自 mutare 表示「改变」。

normal.en: Trans- appears in translate and transport, always marking a crossing over.
normal.cn: trans- 也出现在 translate 与 transport 中，始终标示「跨过去」。

normal.en: The mut part means change, and it also builds mutate and mutation.
normal.cn: mut 部分意为「改变」，它也构成了 mutate 与 mutation。

normal.en: The noun transmutation is the standard word for nuclear change.
normal.cn: 名词 transmutation 是核物理中「嬗变」的标准说法。

normal.en: Transmute something into something is the fixed frame, as with lead into gold.
normal.cn: transmute 某物 into 另一物的框架几乎固定，如 lead into gold（铅变成金）。

normal.en: Compare transform: transform changes shape, transmute changes substance or nature.
normal.cn: 对比 transform：transform 改变形状，transmute 改变物质或本质。

abstract.en: Picture a grey ingot cooling into shining gold in a crucible.
abstract.cn: 想象一块灰色锭子在坩埚里冷却成发亮的黄金。

abstract.en: Picture a neutron nudging a nucleus and the element label changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个中子撞上原子核，元素的标签随之改变。

abstract.en: Picture coal becoming a diamond under pressure.
abstract.cn: 想象煤在压力下变成钻石。

examples.en: Scientists now transmute some elements inside research reactors.
examples.cn: 科学家如今在研究反应堆中让一些元素发生嬗变。

examples.en: The old story of an alchemist who could transmute metals still fascinates children.
examples.cn: 那个能让金属变质的炼金术士的古老故事仍然让孩子们着迷。

examples.en: Writers often transmute personal loss into fiction.
examples.cn: 作家常把个人的失去转化为小说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「trans（穿过）+ mute（哑）」——穿过一片沉默，出来时已换了模样；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Transmute begins with the alchemist changing metal, becomes a real physics change of elements, then covers changes of nature, of energy and ideas, and finally an intransitive becoming.
sensesIntro.cn: transmute 先指炼金术士把金属变成金，后成为物理上真实的元素转变，再用于性质、能量与想法的转化，最后是不及物的「变为」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of lead in a crucible cooling into gold.
core.cn: 核心意象：坩埚里的一块铅冷却成黄金。

branches.en: Changing a substance into another is the alchemical sense.
branches.cn: 把物质变成另一种物质是炼金术义项。

branches.en: Nuclear conversion makes the old dream a physical fact.
branches.cn: 核转变让古老的梦想成为物理事实。

branches.en: Changing a character or essence is the abstract sense.
branches.cn: 改变性质或本质是抽象义项。

branches.en: Turning heat into motion or ideas into action is conversion of form.
branches.cn: 把热变成运动、把想法变成行动，都是形式的转换。

branches.en: Making gold and a harbour becoming shops both end in a new thing.
branches.cn: 造出黄金和港湾变成商铺，最终都落在「新的事物」上。

core_image: 一张书桌横跨两国边线，笔记本摊开在界线两旁
scene: 新闻编辑部的墙面上挂着一张世界地图，几家公司被红圈标了出来。The protest challenged the power of transnational corporations.

senses.title: Extending across national borders
senses.definition: stretching or reaching across the borders of two or more countries
senses.definitionCN: 延伸或抵达两个及以上国家边界的
senses.example: The river forms a transnational basin shared by five countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河构成一个由五个国家共享的跨国流域。
senses.why: The prefix trans- means across, so whatever this word describes physically passes from one nation side to the other.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 trans- 表示「横越」，因此这个词所描述的事物在物理上从一个国家一侧穿到另一侧。

senses.title: Common to several nations
senses.definition: shared by or involving several nations at once, especially a problem or an interest
senses.definitionCN: 由多个国家共同拥有或共同涉及，尤指问题或利益
senses.example: Air pollution is a transnational problem that no single government can solve.
senses.exampleCN: 空气污染是一个任何单一政府都无法解决的跨国问题。
senses.why: Once something is present on both sides of a line, it belongs to more than one nation and is owned jointly rather than separately.
senses.whyCN: 某事物一旦同时存在于边界两边，它就不只属于一个国家，而是被共同拥有，而非各自所有。

senses.title: Operating beyond one country
senses.definition: operating, earning or organizing across several countries rather than inside one
senses.definitionCN: 在多个国家而非单一国家内运营、获利或组织
senses.example: The report tracks the rise of transnational corporations since the nineteen sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告追踪了二十世纪六十年代以来跨国公司的兴起。
senses.why: A company that opens factories in many countries acts on the far side of every border, so the adjective describes its scale, not its address.
senses.whyCN: 一家在多国开设工厂的公司，行动遍及各条边界的另一侧，因此这个形容词描述的是规模，而不是注册地址。

senses.title: Outside national law
senses.definition: lying outside or above the legal authority of any single state
senses.definitionCN: 处于任何单一国家法律权威之外或之上的
senses.example: Drug trafficking is a transnational crime that crosses many legal systems.
senses.exampleCN: 贩毒是一种跨越众多法律体系的跨国犯罪。
senses.why: When a practice slips from one jurisdiction to the next, no single legal system holds it; the word names that gap above the state.
senses.whyCN: 当一种行为从一国的管辖溜到另一国时，没有任何单一法律体系能管住它；这个词就命名了国家之上的那道空隙。

senses.title: Identifying with more than one nation
senses.definition: belonging to or identifying with communities in more than one nation at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时属于或认同多个国家中的群体的
senses.example: Many migrant families live transnational lives, keeping homes in two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 许多移民家庭过着跨国生活，在两个国家都安家。
senses.why: The border-crossing image becomes personal: the person lives on both sides and claims both, so identity itself is transnational.
senses.whyCN: 跨境的画面转到了个人身上：人同时生活在两边并认同两边，于是身份本身也成了跨国的。

intro.en: Transnational is a modern compound of the Latin prefix trans- and the adjective national.
intro.cn: transnational 是现代复合词，由拉丁语前缀 trans- 与形容词 national 组合而成。

items.en: Trans means across or through, and it builds words such as transit and transport.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为「横越、穿过」，构成 transit、transport 等词。

items.en: Natio meant birth or a people sharing a common origin, and it gave nasci, to be born.
items.cn: natio 指出生或同源的人群，其动词 nasci 意为「出生」。

items.en: Nation entered French and English as a word for a people or a country.
items.cn: nation 经由法语进入英语，指一个民族或一个国家。

items.en: National appears in the sixteenth century as the adjective of nation.
items.cn: national 于十六世纪出现，作为 nation 的形容词。

items.en: The exact first date is uncertain, but transnational spreads in the twentieth century with trade, law and migration.
items.cn: 确切首见年代不确定，但 transnational 在二十世纪随贸易、法律与移民而流行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with the prefix trans-; the near-meaning group gathers words about scale and nations.
note.cn: 形近组收以 trans- 前缀构成的词；近义组收与规模和国界有关的词。

entries.definition: an instance of buying, selling or exchanging something
to write down spoken words or convert them to text
to carry meaning from one language into another
between nations; often implies official relations and agreements
entries.definitionCN: 国际的；多指官方关系与协定

entries.definition: involving several countries, and used especially of companies
relating to the whole world rather than particular nations

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin prefix trans- and the common phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语前缀 trans-，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Trans- means across, so transnational means across the nation.
normal.cn: trans- 表示「横越」，因此 transnational 就是「横越国家的」。

normal.en: A transnational corporation has offices in many countries.
normal.cn: a transnational corporation 在许多国家设有分支。

normal.en: Transnational migration keeps families in two countries at once.
normal.cn: transnational migration 让家庭同时身处两个国家。

normal.en: A transnational network links people who live far apart.
normal.cn: a transnational network 把居住遥远的人们连在一起。

normal.en: Compare international: official links between states, while transnational crosses the line itself.
normal.cn: 对比 international：它指国家之间的官方联系，transnational 则指横穿这条线本身。

abstract.en: Picture a desk placed exactly on a border line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张书桌正好摆在边界线上。

abstract.en: Imagine the same cloud of smoke drifting over two countries at once.
abstract.cn: 想象同一团烟雾同时飘过两个国家。

abstract.en: Think of an office block with the same logo in every city.
abstract.cn: 想象同一栋办公楼以相同标志出现在每个城市。

examples.en: Climate change is a transnational challenge for every government.
examples.cn: 气候变化是每个政府都面临的跨国挑战。

examples.en: The bank is accused of helping transnational crime.
examples.cn: 这家银行被指控协助跨国犯罪。

examples.en: Her research looks at transnational families in East Asia.
examples.cn: 她的研究关注东亚的跨国家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯乃神」——穿过（trans）一国又到另一国（nation），就是跨国；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans「横越、穿过」+ natio「出生、同源人群，后指民族国家」→ 英语 nation「国家」→ national「国家的」→ trans- + national 构成 transnational，核心义「横越国界」。

sensesIntro.en: Transnational moves from space to shared problems, to business, to law and finally to personal identity, all built on one image of crossing a border.
sensesIntro.cn: transnational 从空间跨境，到共有的问题，再到企业运营、法律管辖，最后到个人身份，都建立在同一个「越界」的画面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line with something passing straight through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条国境线，有事物径直穿过它。

branches.en: The physical sense: a river, rail line or network crosses borders.
branches.cn: 实体义：河流、铁路或网络跨越国界。

branches.en: The shared sense: a problem or interest belongs to several nations.
branches.cn: 共有义：问题或利益属于多个国家。

branches.en: The business sense: companies operate on the far side of many borders.
branches.cn: 商业义：企业在多条边界的另一侧运营。

branches.en: Problems that cross borders often slip outside the reach of national law.
branches.cn: 跨境的问题往往滑出国家法律的管辖范围。

branches.en: The personal sense: people live and feel at home on both sides.
branches.cn: 个人义：人们在边界两边生活，也把两边都当成家。

definition_zh: 移植；移植手术；移居；迁栽
definition_en: the act of moving something from one place or body to another, especially an organ in surgery
core_image: 一株幼苗被连根挖起，放进新土地里重新安家
scene: 医院的手术前，医生们在灯下核对即将送来的器官。The patient waited two years for a kidney transplantation.
sceneCN: 这里 transplantation 是「移植手术」（第 2 个义项：外科把健康器官接到病人身上）；句意：这位病人等了两年才等到肾移植。

pos.zh: 移植；移植手术；移居；迁栽

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词原形，义为「移植；移栽；迁移」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「移植者；移植器具」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可移植的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「移栽；移植的过程」

senses.title: The act of transplanting a living thing
senses.definition: the act of taking a plant from one place of soil or a pot and setting it into another
senses.definitionCN: 把植物从一处土壤或花盆取出并种到另一处的行为
senses.example: Successful transplantation of seedlings needs damp soil and shade.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗移栽成功需要湿润的土壤和遮阴。
senses.why: The base verb transplant means to plant across, and the noun names that act, so the first image is a seedling lifted and replanted.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词 transplant 意为「横越着栽种」，名词指这一动作，所以第一幅画面是幼苗被挖起后重新栽下。

senses.title: Surgical transplantation of an organ
senses.definition: a medical operation in which an organ or tissue is moved from one body to another
senses.definitionCN: 把器官或组织从一个身体移到另一个身体的外科手术
senses.example: Heart transplantation has become routine in many large hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏移植在许多大医院已成为常规手术。
senses.why: Medicine applies the gardening image to the human body: an organ is lifted out and planted into a patient as a seedling into new soil.
senses.whyCN: 医学把园艺的画面用在人体上：器官被取出，再像幼苗种进新土一样种进病人身上。

senses.title: Resettlement in a new place
senses.definition: the movement of people or communities to settle in a different place
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体迁往另一地定居
senses.example: The transplantation of whole villages to the coast changed their way of life.
senses.exampleCN: 整村迁往沿海改变了他们的生活方式。
senses.why: When people are moved like seedlings, the word treats resettlement as uprooting and replanting, with roots severed and then re-established.
senses.whyCN: 当人被像幼苗一样挪动时，这个词把迁移看作连根拔起再重新扎根，根先被切断，再重新生长。

senses.title: Transfer of culture or practice
senses.definition: the act of taking an idea, custom or system from one setting and adopting it in another
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、习俗或制度从一种环境拿来并在另一种环境中采用
senses.example: The transplantation of foreign legal rules often clashes with local custom.
senses.exampleCN: 外国法律规则的移植常与当地习俗冲突。
senses.why: The plant no longer needs soil: any piece of culture can be dug up and set down elsewhere, with roots that may or may not take.
senses.whyCN: 这里不再需要土壤：任何文化片段都能被挖起、放去别处，根能不能扎下则未必。

senses.title: Moving tissue or cells within one body
senses.definition: the surgical moving of skin or tissue from one part of the same body to another
senses.definitionCN: 把皮肤或组织从同一身体的某处移到另一处的外科操作
senses.example: Skin transplantation from the thigh closed the burn on her arm.
senses.exampleCN: 从大腿取皮移植缝合了她手臂上的烧伤。
senses.why: A narrower medical sense keeps the same image inside one body, where the donor and the recipient are the same patient.
senses.whyCN: 一个较窄的医学义项把同一画面保留在同一个身体里，供体与受体就是同一位病人。

intro.en: Transplantation comes from the verb transplant, built from Latin trans- and plantare, to set a plant in the ground.
intro.cn: transplantation 来自动词 transplant，由拉丁语 trans- 与 plantare「栽种」构成。

items.en: Trans means across, and plantare means to set a plant in the earth.
items.cn: trans 意为「横越」，plantare 意为「把植物种入土中」。

items.en: The verb plantare comes from planta, the sole of the foot or a young shoot, whose own origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 plantare 来自 planta，意为「脚掌」或「嫩芽」，其本身来源不确定。

items.en: Transplantare is recorded in Latin for moving a plant from one place to another.
items.cn: 拉丁语已用 transplantare 指把植物从一处移到另一处。

items.en: The verb transplant enters English from Latin with the gardening sense.
items.cn: 动词 transplant 带着园艺义从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The noun transplantation is recorded from the eighteenth century, first about plants and people.
items.cn: 名词 transplantation 自十八世纪有记录，最初用于植物与人。

items.en: Medical use grows in the twentieth century, when organs could finally be moved from body to body.
items.cn: 医学用法在二十世纪发展起来，那时器官终于能在身体之间移植。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the plant root; the near-meaning group gathers medical and resettlement terms.
note.cn: 形近组收以「栽种」词根构成的词；近义组收医学移植与迁移类词。

a living organism that grows in soil

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin plant root and the medical phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 plant 词根，以及这个词实际出现的医学搭配。

normal.en: Plantare means to plant, so transplantation is planting something in a new place.
normal.cn: plantare 意为「栽种」，因此 transplantation 就是把它栽到新的地方。

normal.en: Organ transplantation moves a healthy organ to a sick body.
normal.cn: organ transplantation 把健康的器官移到病体。

normal.en: Kidney transplantation is one of the most common organ operations.
normal.cn: kidney transplantation 是最常见的器官手术之一。

normal.en: Bone marrow transplantation treats some blood diseases.
normal.cn: bone marrow transplantation 可治疗某些血液病。

normal.en: Compare transplant and transplantation: the verb names the act, the noun names the whole procedure.
normal.cn: 对比 transplant 与 transplantation：动词指动作，名词指整个手术过程。

abstract.en: Picture a seedling lifted with its soil ball and set down again.
abstract.cn: 想象一株幼苗带着土团被提起，又在新处放下。

abstract.en: Imagine a healthy organ travelling in a cool box to a new body.
abstract.cn: 想象一个健康器官装在冷藏箱里，送往新的身体。

abstract.en: Think of a whole village loading carts and driving to a new coast.
abstract.cn: 想象整个村庄装车出发，开往新的海岸。

examples.en: Organ transplantation saves thousands of lives each year.
examples.cn: 器官移植每年挽救数千人的生命。

examples.en: The team studied the transplantation of rice seedlings in flooded fields.
examples.cn: 该团队研究了水田中水稻秧苗的移植。

examples.en: Rapid transplantation of coral helped the reef recover.
examples.cn: 珊瑚的快速移植帮助了珊瑚礁恢复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯扑烂台」——把苗穿过旧地扑到新台子（plant）上，就是移植；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans「横越」+ plantare「栽种」（来自 planta「脚掌、嫩芽」，更早来源不确定）→ transplantare「移栽」→ 英语 transplant（移栽、移植）→ transplantation，核心义「把活的东西挪到新地方扎根」。

sensesIntro.en: Transplantation begins as a garden action, then passes into surgery, into the moving of people, and finally into culture and tissue within one body.
sensesIntro.cn: transplantation 起初是园圃里的动作，随后进入外科手术，再用于人的迁移，最后延伸到文化与同一身体内的组织移植。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seedling is lifted out of old soil and set into new soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：幼苗被挖出旧土，栽进新土。

branches.en: The garden sense is the most concrete: plants moved from soil to soil.
branches.cn: 园艺义最具体：植物从一块土移到另一块土。

branches.en: The medical sense treats organs and tissue as plants moved between bodies or within one body.
branches.cn: 医学义把器官与组织当作在身体之间或体内挪动的植物。

branches.en: The resettlement sense applies the image to whole communities.
branches.cn: 迁移义把这一画面用于整片的社区人群。

branches.en: The cultural sense extends the image to ideas and institutions.
branches.cn: 文化义把画面延伸到观念与制度。

branches.en: All three senses share the risk that roots may fail to take.
branches.cn: 这三种义项都共享同一个风险：根也许扎不下去。

definition_zh: 高空秋千；吊杠；空中飞人表演用的横杆
definition_en: a short horizontal bar hanging by two ropes, used by acrobats high above the ground
core_image: 两根长绳悬下，末端横着一根短杠，人挂在杠上荡到半空
scene: 马戏团的帐篷里灯光打在高处，观众仰头等待。The acrobat swung from the trapeze and caught the hands of her partner.
sceneCN: 这里 trapeze 是「高空秋千」（第 1 个义项：悬挂在高处的体操横杠）；句意：空中飞人在秋千上荡起，接住了搭档的手。

pos.zh: 高空秋千；吊杠；空中飞人用的横杆

derivatives.zh: 由本词加人名后缀 -ist 构成，义为「高空秋千演员」
同源词，来自希腊语「小桌」，几何学上义为「梯形」
同源词，解剖学上指肩背部的「斜方肌」
同源表述，义为「斜方肌」，名称源于其形状

senses.title: A swinging bar for acrobats
senses.definition: a short horizontal bar hung from two ropes, on which acrobats swing and perform high above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 由两根绳子吊起的短横杠，杂技演员在上面荡动并在高处表演
senses.example: The circus rigged a trapeze above the centre ring.
senses.exampleCN: 马戏团在中央舞台上方架起了高空秋千。
senses.why: The Greek word meant a small table, and a trapeze is a flat bar hung like a table in the air.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词意为「小桌」，trapeze 就是像桌子一样被吊到空中的平横杠。

senses.title: The whole trapeze act
senses.definition: the performance or art of swinging and catching on such bars, as a circus act
senses.definitionCN: 在吊杠上荡摆与接人的表演或技艺，作为一种马戏节目
senses.example: Her trapeze won the audience a standing ovation.
senses.exampleCN: 她的高空秋千表演赢得了观众起立鼓掌。
senses.why: Once the bar exists, the trick performed on it takes the same name, so the act and the equipment share one word.
senses.whyCN: 横杠出现之后，在它上面表演的技艺也沿用了这个名字，于是器械与节目共用一个词。

senses.title: A hanging bar in gymnastics
senses.definition: a hanging bar of the same kind, used in training or gymnastics as well as in circuses
senses.definitionCN: 同类悬挂横杠，除马戏外也用于体操或训练
senses.example: The young gymnast practised a handstand on the trapeze.
senses.exampleCN: 那位少年体操运动员在吊杠上练习倒立。
senses.why: Any hanging bar of the same flat shape is a trapeze, so indoor gyms took the word from the circus.
senses.whyCN: 任何形状相同、悬挂着的平横杠都叫 trapeze，因此室内体操馆也从马戏那里接过了这个词。

senses.title: A ship rigging swing
senses.definition: a bar hung in a ship rigging or on a yard, on which sailors or performers swing
senses.definitionCN: 挂在船索具或横桁上的横杠，供水手或表演者荡摆
senses.example: Sailors used a trapeze to move from mast to hull at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们利用船上吊杠在海上从桅杆移到船身。
senses.why: Ships already hang bars in their rigging, and sailors borrowed the circus name for a bar of the same make.
senses.whyCN: 船只本就在索具上挂着横杠，水手便借用了马戏的名字来称呼同样构造的杠。

senses.title: A sailing crew position
senses.definition: a position on a sailing boat where a crew member hangs out over the water on a wire to balance the boat
senses.definitionCN: 帆船上一种位置，船员借助钢丝悬挂在水面之上以平衡船身
senses.example: He leaned out on the trapeze to keep the dinghy level.
senses.exampleCN: 他悬挂在吊杠上向外探身，让小艇保持平稳。
senses.why: The sailing sense borrows the name again, because a crew member hangs out from a wire just as an artist hangs from a bar.
senses.whyCN: 帆船义再度借用这个名字，因为船员悬挂在钢丝上，正像演员悬挂在横杠上。

senses.title: A four-sided figure in geometry
senses.definition: in British usage, a four-sided flat figure with a pair of parallel sides
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中，有一组对边平行的四边形
senses.example: The floor of the stage formed a trapeze in the old design.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧方案中，舞台地面呈梯形。
senses.why: The old table shape never disappeared from geometry, so the flat four-sided figure kept the ancient word.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「小桌」形状在几何学里从未消失，因此这种平面四边形保留了那个古老的词。

intro.en: Trapeze comes from a Greek word for a small table, and the circus sense names the bar from its table-like shape.
intro.cn: trapeze 来自希腊语中表示「小桌」的词，杂技义根据横杠像小桌的形状而得名。

items.en: Trapezion is a small table, built from trapeza, a table.
items.cn: 希腊语 trapezion 意为「小桌」，由 trapeza「桌子」构成。

items.en: Latin took the word as trapezium, a four-sided figure.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 trapezium 引入该词，指四边形。

items.en: Euclid used trapezion for a four-sided figure, so the shape sense is ancient.
items.cn: 欧几里得用 trapezion 指四边形，所以几何义由来已久。

items.en: English geometry adopts trapezium and trapezoid in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语几何学在十六世纪引入 trapezium 与 trapezoid。

items.en: The circus sense is recorded in the nineteenth century, when the hanging bar was called a trapeze from its flat table-like top.
items.cn: 杂技义在十九世纪有记录，吊杠因顶部平得像小桌而被称为 trapeze。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Greek table root; the near-meaning group gathers circus and hanging-apparatus terms.
note.cn: 形近组收同出希腊语「小桌」词根的词；近义组收杂技与悬挂器械类词。

entries.definition: a four-sided figure; in British English one with no parallel sides
entries.definitionCN: 四边形；英式英语中指无平行边的四边形

entries.definition: a four-sided figure with at least one pair of parallel sides
entries.definitionCN: 至少有一组平行边的四边形

entries.definition: the large muscle across the upper back and neck
entries.definitionCN: 斜方肌；覆盖上背与颈部的肌肉

entries.definition: a seat hanging by ropes on which a person moves back and forth
a tightrope stretched high above the ground
a pair of hanging gymnastic rings

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek table root and the circus phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的希腊语「小桌」词根，以及这个词实际出现的马戏搭配。

normal.en: Trapezion is a small table: the bar is a flat table hung in the air.
normal.cn: trapezion 意为小桌：那根杠就是悬在空中、平平的小桌。

normal.en: A flying trapeze sends the artist across the ring.
normal.cn: a flying trapeze 让演员横越整个场地。

normal.en: A trapeze artist trains for years to catch a partner in mid-air.
normal.cn: a trapeze artist 要训练多年才能在半空接住搭档。

normal.en: Compare trapezoid: same Greek root, a flat four-sided shape.
normal.cn: 对比 trapezoid：同一希腊词根，指平面四边形。

normal.en: Sailing crews also call the wire position a trapeze.
normal.cn: 帆船船员也把悬挂在外的钢丝位置叫作 trapeze。

abstract.en: Picture a bar swinging over a dark circus tent.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横杠在昏暗的马戏帐篷上方摆动。

abstract.en: Imagine a body letting go of one bar and reaching for another.
abstract.cn: 想象身体松开一根杠，伸向另一根杠。

abstract.en: Think of a trainer holding steady at the bar during a handstand.
abstract.cn: 想象训练者在杠上做倒立时保持平稳。

examples.en: The trapeze hung thirty feet above the sawdust ring.
examples.cn: 高空秋千悬在锯末场地上方约九米处。

examples.en: Catching a partner on a flying trapeze takes perfect timing.
examples.cn: 在飞人秋千上接住搭档需要完美的时机掌握。

examples.en: The crew used a trapeze to shift the captain across the deck.
examples.cn: 船员们用吊杠把船长送到甲板另一侧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戳皮兹」——一根皮条绳把横杠吊起，人在上面荡，就是高空秋千；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 trapeza「桌子」→ 指小形式 trapezion「小桌」→ 拉丁语 trapezium（四边形）→ 英语，十九世纪马戏中把平行的吊杠比作小桌，遂称 trapeze；核心义「悬在高处的桌上横杠」。

sensesIntro.en: Trapeze begins as a circus bar, becomes the act itself, then spreads to gymnastics, ships and sailing, and keeps a distant geometric cousin.
sensesIntro.cn: trapeze 起初指马戏横杠，后指表演本身，再延伸至体操、船上与帆船，并保留一个远亲的几何义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short bar hangs from two ropes and swings high in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：短横杠由两根绳吊起，在高处摆动。

branches.en: The bar itself is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 横杠本身是基本的实体义。

branches.en: The act sense names the performance built around the bar.
branches.cn: 表演义指围绕这根杠展开的节目。

branches.en: The equipment spreads to gymnastics halls and to ships.
branches.cn: 器械义从马戏延伸到体操馆和船上。

branches.en: Sailing borrows the name for the wire position a crew member hangs from.
branches.cn: 帆船借用这个名字指船员悬挂的钢丝位置。

branches.en: Geometry keeps the old table-shaped figure, a cousin far from the circus.
branches.cn: 几何义保留着古老的「小桌」形状图形，是与马戏相距很远的亲戚。

intro.en: Trapeze is a Greek loanword; its family is built with English and Latin-Greek suffixes.
intro.cn: trapeze 是希腊语借词；它的词族由英语与希腊拉丁语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek trapeza means a table, and trapezion a small table; Latin took the shape as trapezium.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 trapeza 意为桌子，trapezion 意为小桌；拉丁语以 trapezium 表示形状。

items.exampleCN: trapeza 是基础词。

items.example: It forms trapezion, a small table.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trapezion，即小桌。
拉丁语保留了这一形状名称。

items.example: The spelling marks the circus bar.
items.exampleCN: 这一拼写标记了马戏横杠。
它构成 trapezist。
它构成 trapezoid。
它构成 trapezius。

items.meaning: a tightrope high above the ground
items.example: High wire is the cousin act.
items.exampleCN: high wire 是相近的表演名称。
